content:
Laredo College's Pathways to Success Center works each day with adults taking the next step toward a high school equivalency credential, English-language skills or workforce training, according to the college.

The center offers free English as a Second Language (ESL) classes, GED preparation and ESL for Professionals, according to a column by center director Cindy Elizalde published by the college.

GED instruction covers the four exam subjects: Reasoning Through Language Arts, Mathematics, Science and Social Studies. Morning and evening classes are offered in person or online, with free instructional materials and GED test vouchers for eligible participants.

Earning a GED opens doors to postsecondary education, workforce training and employment. Graduates can pursue industry-recognized credentials in areas such as CDL, Patient Care Technician, Bookkeeping, Payroll or Medical Administration, and the Texas Workforce Commission can help eligible students cover the cost of training.

Others may decide to pursue a certificate, associate or bachelor's degree at Laredo College. The center also helps students build workplace skills including communication, digital literacy, problem-solving and professionalism.

To reach the Pathways to Success Center, call the Ft. McIntosh Campus at (956) 721-5436 or the South Campus at (956) 794-4436.

Sources: Laredo College.
